QF.id: Evaluating Fund Performance and Fund Selection_46

question.text: Kumar's fund returned 12% while the peer group average was 10% and the benchmark returned 11%. How should his fund's performance be evaluated?

answer.text: Poor performance because 12% is low in absolute terms
Average performance as it only slightly beat the benchmark
The fund outperformed both the benchmark and the peer group average on return, though a full evaluation should also compare risk
Performance cannot be evaluated without knowing the risk-free rate

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook says fund performance may be evaluated relative to benchmark performance and peer group performance. Here, 12% beats the 11% benchmark and the 10% peer-group average, so the fund outperformed on both return comparisons. The Trap: 12% is not poor in absolute terms in this context, beating the benchmark is meaningful (not 'average'), and the question does not require a risk-free rate to make a return comparison. Note: The same workbook also cautions that peer outperformance may involve higher risk, so a complete evaluation should consider return alongside risk, not return alone.
